question: Can Bayesian updating, exponential-weights regret, concentration inequalities, repeated-game equilibrium, posterior sampling, and boosting be derived as different readings of one constrained repeated game's exact information-accounting identity?

key_findings.claim: Gibbs or Bayes weights are the Bellman equalizer of a game whose terminal payoff is the best comparator gain inside a relative-entropy ball and whose one-step adversarial budget is a rescaled centered cumulant-generating function.
key_findings.evidence: Theorem 3.2 shows that for Gibbs play p equal to the gradient of the log-partition potential, every feasible centered move changes the potential by exactly eta times Q_eta(p,z), independent of its direction and bounded by eta q_t. Proposition 2.2 identifies the terminal support function with the optimized Gibbs variational form.

key_findings.claim: Variable-temperature exponential weights has an exact three-term regret ledger rather than merely a variance-based upper bound.
key_findings.evidence: Theorem 4.3 proves pathwise for every comparator that regret equals the sum of eta_t Q_t, the retempering drift from changing log-partition potentials, and terminal relative-entropy transport. For non-increasing scales the drift is non-positive; variance and range enter only as looser bounds on Q_t.

key_findings.claim: A predictable intrinsic-time schedule attains a pathwise square-root regret rate without knowing the horizon or total difficulty in advance.
key_findings.evidence: Theorem 4.4 brackets the cumulative intrinsic-time loss by a two-sided square-root envelope. With C equal to 1 divided by square root of 2, regret is at most 2 square root of 2 times sqrt(Gamma V_T), plus Gamma and the largest one-round Q term; Lemma 4.5 gives one-round witnesses showing both edge terms are necessary for this discretization.

key_findings.claim: The same ledger recovers standard structures in self-play, posterior sampling, and boosting while identifying their exact information costs.
key_findings.evidence: Sections 6, 8, and 9 apply the common transport identity: repeated play yields an intrinsic-time regret and equilibrium ledger; Thompson sampling equals deterministic exponential weights in expectation plus a mean-zero sampling martingale; and binary pressure-target boosting yields the exact AdaBoost exponential-loss identity before the usual quadratic relaxation.

key_findings.claim: The terminal comparator problem is exactly a concentration problem: a relative-entropy budget measures how far a change of measure can move the mean score.
key_findings.evidence: Proposition 2.2 writes the support function of the KL ball as an infimum over scale of Gamma divided by eta plus the scaled log moment-generating function, making the inverse Cramer transform an equality rather than a tail-bound relaxation.

method.core_idea: Define a zero-sum sequential game directly in centered excess-score coordinates, use a KL-bounded comparator class as terminal payoff, and use the centered cumulant-generating function at the learner's scale as nature's per-round information budget.
method.mechanism: The learner chooses a mixture; nature chooses a mean-zero score redistribution whose rescaled centered cumulant-generating function Q is budgeted. Gibbs tilting of the prior makes the scale-dependent log-partition function a Bellman potential. One-step potential transport is exact, so telescoping exposes immediate information loss, scale-change drift, and terminal comparator transport. Choosing scale from realized cumulative Q produces an adaptive schedule; changing the score statistic or observation estimator carries the same algebra into bandits, testing, self-play, Thompson sampling, and boosting.
assumptions: The main construction uses a finite action set and a strictly positive prior.
Comparator complexity is measured by KL divergence from that prior.
Nature's move is centered under the learner's mixture and measured using the chosen sufficient statistic; no external true loss is required by the abstract game.
Scale schedules are predictable from past observations; sign control of retempering uses non-increasing scales.
Applications to partial information require appropriate importance-weighted or likelihood-ratio score estimators.

techniques.role: Measures each adversarial move at the current exponential scale and reduces to half the variance only in the small-scale limit.
Chooses the unique interior mixture that makes the one-step log-partition increment depend only on nature's information budget.
Interpolates from the prior mean to best-expert comparison and turns terminal regret into an inverse large-deviation problem.
Accounts exactly for changing learning rates by measuring the difference between consecutive log-partition potentials at a fixed state.
Sets the next scale from cumulative realized Q rather than elapsed rounds or a pre-known horizon.
Decomposes comparator gain into immediate cumulant loss plus reduction in KL distance to the updated posterior.
Reverses move order and solves for the scale that makes a chosen per-round information or margin constraint active.

evaluations.setting: Fixed-scale concentration game with cumulative intrinsic-time budget V and comparator KL budget Gamma.
evaluations.result: The Gibbs equalizer gives Gamma/eta + eta V; optimizing eta gives 2 sqrt(Gamma V), and Proposition 4.2 shows this constant-scale value is exact from a finite horizon onward under its stated non-saturation conditions.
evaluations.baseline: Standard sub-Gaussian and exponential-weights analyses obtain the same functional form as an inequality after replacing exact Q by variance or range proxies.

evaluations.setting: Predictable variable-rate exponential weights with cumulative realized intrinsic time V_T and maximum one-step density Q*_T.
evaluations.result: At C = 1/sqrt(2), regret is at most 2 sqrt(2 Gamma V_T) plus O(Gamma + Q*_T), without knowing V_T or T in advance.
evaluations.baseline: Oracle constant scale reaches 2 sqrt(Gamma V) but requires total V as an input.

evaluations.setting: Posterior sampling with predictable loss sequences.
evaluations.result: Expected sampled regret exactly equals deterministic exponential-weights regret; all realization-level discrepancy is a mean-zero sampling martingale with variance-clock concentration.
evaluations.baseline: Deterministic Gibbs or exponential-weights play under the same score and scale sequence.

evaluations.setting: Binary weak learners in the pressure-game specialization.
evaluations.result: The AdaBoost coefficient gives exact loss decrease sum_t -0.5 log(1 - 4 gamma_t^2); relaxing -log(1-x) by x recovers the classical exp(-2 gamma^2 T) rate for a uniform edge.
evaluations.baseline: Classical AdaBoost's quadratic edge bound, which discards a per-round gap beginning at order gamma_t^4.

limitations: Author-stated: the contribution is conceptual and supplies no new algorithm by itself.
Author-stated: the framework is restricted to entropic geometry; non-entropic regularizers are left to Fenchel-game approaches.
Author-stated: the per-round-capped minimax game's exact value remains open beyond the cumulative-budget result.
Author-stated: the adaptive leading constant leaves a remaining square-root log K gap in the bandit specialization.
Reviewer inference: the breadth of specializations rests on choosing a suitable sufficient statistic; a poor estimator can dominate the exact accounting without violating it.
Reviewer inference: finite-action proofs and exact identities do not by themselves establish computational tractability for enormous or continuous comparator classes.
failure_modes: A scale that increases can make the retempering drift positive, removing the favorable sign used in the adaptive regret bound.
A single large intrinsic-time jump forces the Q*_T edge term and can dominate the square-root behavior.
Heavy-tailed or importance-weighted partial-information scores can make Q large even when ordinary variance estimates look benign.
At the saturated comparator budget or at very short horizons, terminal alignment can make the Bellman upper envelope strictly larger than the exact minimax value.
Posterior sampling preserves the deterministic value only in expectation; its realized path retains an unavoidable sampling martingale.
reusable_insights: Treat variance and range bounds as approximations to a scale-dependent cumulant quantity, not as the primitive uncertainty measure.
When changing learning rate, explicitly account for the change of potential at the same state instead of hiding it inside loose stability terms.
Choose learning rates on an intrinsic information clock rather than a round clock when difficulty is heterogeneous across time.
A comparator-class support function can simultaneously encode regret, robust change of measure, and concentration geometry.
Randomized posterior play can be analyzed as deterministic Bayes plus one explicit martingale, separating information cost from sampling cost.
open_questions: Can an equally exact concentration game be built for non-entropic mirror maps and continuous actions?
What is the exact minimax value of the per-round-capped game for horizons beyond one?
Can the adaptive bandit specialization close its remaining square-root log K factor while retaining exact intrinsic-time accounting?
Which practical algorithms benefit from estimating the full centered cumulant rather than a variance proxy?
Can the pressure-target and retempering games be combined into stable online scale control under unbounded scores?

competitive_landscape.title: Adaptive Bayes Exactly Tracks Information over Intrinsic Time
competitive_landscape.difference: The author's earlier paper gives exact adaptive Bayes and multiplicative-weights regret decompositions over intrinsic time; this paper places that ledger inside an explicit constrained minimax game, derives the Bellman equalizer and terminal concentration functional, and extends the interpretation across equilibrium, testing, sampling, and boosting.

competitive_landscape.title: A Drifting-Games Analysis for Online Learning and Applications to Boosting
competitive_landscape.difference: Luo and Schapire design online algorithms by relaxing backward-induction potentials in drifting games; the concentration game uses the entropic log-partition as an exact one-step value identity and treats variance or range potentials as downstream relaxations.

competitive_landscape.title: Follow the Leader If You Can, Hedge If You Must
competitive_landscape.difference: AdaHedge tunes Hedge's learning rate through the mixability gap to combine stochastic and worst-case performance; this paper derives scale adaptation from cumulative rescaled centered cumulants and isolates an explicit retempering drift.

competitive_landscape.title: Second-order Quantile Methods for Experts and Combinatorial Games
competitive_landscape.difference: Squint aggregates a range of learning rates to obtain simultaneous second-order and quantile bounds; this paper keeps a single predictable temperature, obtains an exact pathwise ledger in KL geometry, and recovers variance-based second-order rates only after relaxing its cumulant term.

novelty_assessment: Reviewer inference: the exact adaptive decomposition itself is substantially developed in the author's immediately preceding arXiv paper, so the new contribution here is chiefly the concentration-game formulation and the claim that one Bellman value identity unifies comparator concentration, online regret, self-play, posterior sampling, and boosting. Relative to drifting games, AdaHedge, and Squint, the distinctive element is treating the rescaled centered cumulant as nature's primitive budget and deriving variance-aware results as relaxations. The result is a broad conceptual unification rather than a demonstrated new practical algorithm.
reviewer_notes: The 60-page full text, discussion, theorem statements, and cited applications were checked. Quantitative constants were verified on pages 8 and 10-12. Primary arXiv records were used for the four closest comparisons. Claims of uniqueness and exactness are reported under the paper's finite-action, positive-prior, entropic assumptions.
